A cheap and fantastic way to reduce your power bill is to put your fridge and freezer on a timer. Set it to turn on an hour before you usually wake up and turn off an hour after you leave for work. Then on an hour before you get home until an hour after you go to bed. For me, the cycle looked like this:

0000-0600 Off

0600-0930 On

0930-1500 Off

1500-2200 On

2200-0000 Off

Note: This only works if your fridge/freezer have good seals, so that the cool temperature doesn't leak out at a ridiculous rate.

As you can see my fridge/freezer were only on for 10.5 hours each day, less than half of what it was beforehand! It saved me $100-$150 every 3 months on my power bill (Australia).

The idea is that during times that the fridge is likely to be opened the motor is running, keeping the temperature down. At night and when you're at work when it isn't being opened the seals should maintain the temperature within a degree or 2 (Celsius).
